- 模板 `map-base-v1`；manifest SHA-256 `9b7f711c65cd10af31a70b9a61b63867fcafaf7c1680a335e3240419c893228e`；城市 pathD SHA-256 `af1155e6412a695579bf8cc7574d4b476c84f9f211840630706c3bc376139a35`。固定 referenceFrame 对象详见同目录清单，viewBox 为 `[631.5161894736842,43.72428947368422,474.35592105263163,474.35592105263163]`，完整画作对应参考帧全幅，不使用旧cover、mapFocus或zoom。

## 文化依据与风险

- [中国非遗网：剪纸（烟台剪纸）图集](https://www.ihchina.cn/tuji_details/20256.html)：支持烟台剪纸与戏曲窗裙文化线索，不证明新图复制或对应任一历史作品。

原创戏曲人物、戏服、头饰、窗景、海景与建筑，不对应真实演员、演出或具体地点。以下风险仍需实际遮罩检查：
- 头饰、长袖、人物身体和边角纸刻可能被市域边缘及凹口切断，须实拼检查脸与身的连续性。
- B版装饰和窗口格较密，需检查缩小后形象辨识及是否产生误读字形。
- 标签覆盖、邻区配色、手机尺度尚待原SVG实拼验证。
- 数据的行政边界、地图审定与公开许可尚待核实。

## 实际完整提示词

### A 水墨
Use case: stylized-concept. One complete square Yantai cultural artwork for an internal experimental Shandong map.
INPUT IMAGE 1 is the actual Yantai outline template, for composition guidance only. The entire square reference including the outside margin maps to the full square output without crop, zoom, stretching, shifting or rotation. An exact vector mask will cut the complete finished picture later. Do not trace or depict any city boundary, template flat fill, margin, map shape or guide mark. Make a full-bleed, richly composed artwork extending naturally to all four canvas edges.

Show ONE original imaginary traditional Chinese opera character inspired by the expressive shapes of Yantai paper-cut window decorations. Do not copy a specific cut-paper artwork, actual opera performer, historical portrait or named scene. Give the character a bold expressive face, readable simplified head ornament, and a broad compact torso; place the face and its crucial identifying features near x=0.50, y=0.462 of the FULL reference square, within the broad central mainland of the template, with the figure's body extending downward. Do not place essential head ornaments on tiny offshore fragments, narrow tips or outside the upper edge. Flowing sleeves, window-curtain forms, floral motifs, imagined courtyard and hanging tassels can be subordinate and cropped naturally. The character should still read clearly at small map size, with large graphic shapes rather than many tiny details. Keep the scene original and imaginative, not a historical claim. No city outlines, geographic patches, text, Chinese characters, lettering, digits, seals, signatures, watermarks, labels, frame or UI. Style A: elegant Chinese ink-and-wash painting on textured xuan paper, controlled sweeping black brushwork, light cinnabar blush and warm ivory, dynamic theatrical gesture with generous painted tonal variation; no common blue-green landscape. Intricate elements remain subordinate to bold large forms; textures extend through the full canvas.

### B 工艺融合
Use case: stylized-concept. One complete square Yantai cultural artwork for an internal experimental Shandong map.
INPUT IMAGE 1 is the actual Yantai outline template, for composition guidance only. The entire square reference including the outside margin maps to the full square output without crop, zoom, stretching, shifting or rotation. An exact vector mask will cut the complete finished picture later. Do not trace or depict any city boundary, template flat fill, margin, map shape or guide mark. Make a full-bleed, richly composed artwork extending naturally to all four canvas edges.

Show ONE original imaginary traditional Chinese opera character inspired by the expressive shapes of Yantai paper-cut window decorations. Do not copy a specific cut-paper artwork, actual opera performer, historical portrait or named scene. Give the character a bold expressive face, readable simplified head ornament, and a broad compact torso; place the face and its crucial identifying features near x=0.50, y=0.462 of the FULL reference square, within the broad central mainland of the template, with the figure's body extending downward. Do not place essential head ornaments on tiny offshore fragments, narrow tips or outside the upper edge. Flowing sleeves, window-curtain forms, floral motifs, imagined courtyard and hanging tassels can be subordinate and cropped naturally. The character should still read clearly at small map size, with large graphic shapes rather than many tiny details. Keep the scene original and imaginative, not a historical claim. No city outlines, geographic patches, text, Chinese characters, lettering, digits, seals, signatures, watermarks, labels, frame or UI. Style B: distinctive Yantai-inspired handmade folk papercut language: layered vermilion cut paper, visible fiber, nuanced hand-cut negative shapes and restrained shallow paper shadows against warm cream and ink-brown, like a refined piece of handmade theatre. Large red shapes, deliberate openwork and a readable human silhouette; not a flat clip-art icon, glossy plastic or an exact reproduction of any actual paper-cut. Integrate the whole scene across the square edges.
